title: Reversing the invoice keeps the core charge and credit rows
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as a user with the Part sales -> Create & Edit permission, on the build under test.
  2. A customer to sell to exists; if none does, create one first: Customers -> New Customer (e.g. "4 Star Truck Repair").
  3. A part sale created on or after the release, carrying a part with a core charge. Seed it with these standard steps:
  4. ↳ Open Part Sales from the main menu and start a New Part Sale; select the customer (e.g. "4 Star Truck Repair").
  5. ↳ On the Parts tab, click Add Part; set the Description (e.g. "Water Pump") and the Sell Price to a test amount (e.g. $517.55).
  6. ↳ In the Core column of that row, enter a Core Charge greater than 0 (e.g. $79.99), then save the row.
  7. ↳ Order the part, then Receive it (special-order) or Pick it (inventory), so Return Core becomes available.
  8. Return the core, then Create Invoice on the sale. Do NOT apply any payment.
custom_steps:
1. On the invoiced sale, reverse the invoice (the Reverse invoice action).
  2. Confirm the invoice and its customer transaction are deleted and the sale returns to its rows.
  3. Read whether the Core charge and Core credit rows are still present, and whether the Core credit blocked the reversal.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Reversing the invoice deletes the invoice and its customer transaction and the sale returns to the rows it was carrying: the Core charge stands and, if the return still stands, so does the Core credit.
  • The Core credit row does not block the reversal - reversal is refused only when a payment is applied; the Core credit is a row on the document, not a customer credit.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-9667 (Founder Mode Batch #1); story SV-10262 (Story 1, Return a core on a part sale); Part Sales Update v1 PRD (Confluence 867434569), Story 1; design canvas boards Cores_*/Document_*; read 30 Sep 2026. Source-verified 30 September 2026; not yet build-verified.
